paper_id: Li et al. - 2008 - Capacity of large scale wireless networks under Gaussian channel model
title: Capacity of Large Scale Wireless Networks Under Gaussian Channel Model
motivation: Need to estimate achievable throughput when randomly deploying n wireless nodes in sensor network applications
problem_framing: Asymptotic multicast capacity of random wireless networks under Gaussian channel with n nodes, ns sessions, k receivers each
key_insight: Percolation theory enables constructing highway system that achieves per-flow rate Ω(√n/(ns√k)), generalizing unicast capacity results
method_signature: Bond percolation on grid forms highways; Euclidean spanning tree for multicast; TDMA scheduling on short hops
evaluation_criteria: Feasible per-flow rate with high probability; asymptotic order Θ(f(n)) definition with constants c, c'
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Only proved for k=O(n/(log n)^(2α+6)); upper bound for arbitrary k remains open; network coding not considered
evidence_for_taste: closes the gap when Gaussian link model is used
we leave it as future work
